questions.question: Why do people start a SIP, and what do they expect to happen?
questions.headline: Among the 2,927 items that say why the person started, the most common reasons are long term wealth (41%) and specific goal (25%). Among the 2,141 that say what they expected, steady long term growth (72%) leads, followed by high or quick returns (14%) and safe like fd (9%).

stats.label: Stated reason for starting (n=2927 items that say why)
What they expect (n=2141 items that say)
Who influenced them (n=3312 items that say)

questions.question: What changes in their behaviour in the months after starting?
questions.headline: Among 1,208 items that describe a change after starting, stayed consistent (25%), paused or stopped (24%) and switched fund or platform (22%) lead. Items showing a drop-off signal make up 3% of 0-3 month posts, 3% of 3-12 month posts and 6% of 12+ month posts, but few posts state the stage, so treat this as a pattern to test.

questions.question: What leads investors to pause, reduce or stop a SIP?
questions.headline: Among 230 drop-off signals that give a reason: understanding & expectation (34%), SIP broke (payment / mandate / app) (24%), money or life event (23%), pulled elsewhere (19%). Falling returns matter, but they are one reason among several.

stats.label: Stated reason among drop-off signals (n=230 that state one; 334 drop-offs in total)

questions.question: What separates investors who continue from those who quietly drop off?
questions.headline: Visible drop-offs show more confusion, anxiety or frustration than people who continue (63% vs 33%). Among those who state an expectation, 77% of continuing investors expect steady long-term growth, against 74% of drop-offs. People who lapse silently never appear in public text, so this contrast cannot show what separates them.

stats.label: People continuing (n=3749): where they go when unsure
Visible drop-offs (n=334): where they go when unsure

questions.question: How do these patterns differ across user segments (income stability, age, source of money, who influenced them)?
questions.headline: Differences are small and rest on few items. Share showing a drop-off signal: irregular income 6.8% (n=74), variable pay 6.5% (n=123), fixed salary 2.9% (n=730). Only about 13% of items state income at all.

questions.question: What unmet needs emerge consistently across conversations?
questions.headline: Across 8,871 relevant items the biggest unmet needs are trusted human help (34%), plain language explanation (12%), reassurance whats normal (3%). Among first-year items: trusted human help (54%), plain language explanation (13%), reassurance whats normal (7%). Among drop-off signals: trusted human help (25%), flexible pause or reduce (21%), plain language explanation (17%).

stats.label: All relevant items (n=8871)
First-year items (n=774)
Drop-off signals (n=334)
